                     </ns0:gap> Jer. 23.16. Chap. 24.4. Rom. 16.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Eph. 5.6. Col. 2.8. 1 Joh. 4.1.</ns0:note> Beware of false prophets, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mic. 3.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 2 Tim. 3.5.</ns0:note> which come to you in sheeps clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Term <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> in holy Writ, is of larger Extent than to signify only such as <ns0:hi>foretold things to come,</ns0:hi> others also who taught the People, pretending Authority from God so to do, were called Prophets. Thus <ns0:hi>Ber-Iesus, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.6. is called a <ns0:hi>false Prophet.</ns0:hi> A <ns0:hi>false Prophet</ns0:hi> is of the same Signifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cancy with a <ns0:hi>false Teacher.</ns0:hi> Against those our Saviour cauti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oneth his Hearers, as being the most <ns0:hi>fatal,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>dangerous</ns0:hi> Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies to <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Holiness.</ns0:hi> Some of them indeed come in <ns0:hi>Sheeps Clothing,</ns0:hi> under very fair pretences, and a fair shew of Religion and Strictness, but they are <ns0:hi>Ravening Wolves,</ns0:hi> as dange<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous to your Souls, as Ravenous Wolves are to a Flock of Sheep.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 6.4<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Even so <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 12.33.</ns0:note> every good tree bringeth forth good fruit, but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>can</ns0:hi> a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:229" />19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.10. Joh. 15.2.6.</ns0:note> Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewen down and cast into the fire.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.<ns0:note place="bottom">A proper effect Discovereth the Cause: Lest his Disciples should ask, how shall we distinguish <ns0:hi>True,</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>false Tea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chers?</ns0:hi> Our Saviour tells them. <ns0:hi>By their fuits you shall know them.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour sends not his Disciples to inquire into the Truth of their <ns0:hi>Mission,</ns0:hi> whether that more <ns0:hi>Internal</ns0:hi> from God, of which they could not judge, or more <ns0:hi>External from Men,</ns0:hi> who may err and send out those whom God never sent, but you shall know them (saith our Saviour) by their faithful, o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> unfaithful Discharge of their Duty: If they be true Teachers by their discharging the Ministry, in a faith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Revelation of the Mind and Will of God, or by their Holy Life, living as <ns0:hi>ensamples</ns0:hi> to the Flock, by their Fruits of <ns0:hi>true Doctrine,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Holy Life</ns0:hi> by the Discharge of their Ministry in good Conscience; for it is with Men, as it is with the Trees, good Trees bring forth good Fruit, corrupt Trees bring forth evil Fruit. If Men have the Root of the matter, the Seed of God abiding in them, they will in every Relation, bring forth the Fruits of <ns0:hi>Truth,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Holiness</ns0:hi>: If they have not, they will bring forth <ns0:hi>Error,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Wickedness.</ns0:hi> From whence we may learn, that our Lord expecteth from his People such a knowledge of the Scriptures, as they may be able to discern Truth from Falshood, and such a Diligence as to search the Scriptures, whether those things which their Teachers deliver to them, be according to them or no, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 17.11. not taking divine Truths upon Trust, nor believing any thing, because Dictated by Teachers, using their <ns0:hi>Teachers</ns0:hi> not as Dictates, but only as <ns0:hi>helpers of their Faith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Hos. 8.2. Luk. 6.46. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 13.25. Act. 19.13. Jam. 1.22.</ns0:note> Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he that doth the will of my Father which is in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some that say unto Christ, <ns0:hi>Lord, Lord,</ns0:hi> shall be saved, being the true Disciples of Christ, but <ns0:hi>every one</ns0:hi> that owneth Christ by an external Profession, as his <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> every one that prayeth tho he doth it often, and with some appearing <ns0:hi>Zeal</ns0:hi> and importunity shall not be saved; nor doth by it approve himself a true Disciple of Christ, but he alone who doth in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deavour to fulfil the whole Will of God, both by <ns0:hi>Faith and Holiness, Rom<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 2.13. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>Iam.</ns0:hi> 1.22.23. 3. True Religion lyes in Obedience to the whole Will of God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Many will say unto me in that day, Lord, have we not <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 24.4. Joh. 11.51. 1 Cor. 13.2.</ns0:note> prophecied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils, and in thy name done many wonderful works.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 13.25.27.</ns0:note> And then I will profess unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 25.12.</ns0:note> I ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver knew you, depart from me ye that work iniquity.<ns0:note place="bottom">That by <ns0:hi>that day</ns0:hi> is to be understood, <ns0:hi>the day of Iudgment is</ns0:hi> generally agreed by Interpreters: <ns0:hi>We have Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecied in thy Name.</ns0:hi> That is, revealed thy Will unto Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, and in thy Name, that is by thy Authority, and Power cast out <ns0:hi>Devils,</ns0:hi> and done many <ns0:hi>wonderful Works,</ns0:hi> that is, wrought many miraculous Operations, in the <ns0:hi>Old Testament</ns0:hi> we find <ns0:hi>Balaam</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> Prophecying, who were both wicked Men: <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> was sent out (under the <ns0:hi>New Testament</ns0:hi>) both to <ns0:hi>Preach,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>work Miracles.</ns0:hi> So as none from Gifts, no not the most eminent and extraordinary Gifts, can conclude the Goodness of his State, or any special favour with God, <ns0:hi>I will profess,</ns0:hi> that is, I will openly declare to them. <ns0:hi>I never knew you,</ns0:hi> that is so as to approve you, or take Pleasure in you: <ns0:hi>Depart from me, you Workers of iniquity,</ns0:hi> Mat. 25.41.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Therefore <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 6.47.</ns0:note> whosoever heareth these say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings of mine, and doth them, I will liken him to a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and did beat on that house, and it fell not, for it was founded upon a rock.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour maketh frequent use of that Ancient way of instructing People by Similitudes and Parables, which by their easie incurring into the Senses, give advantage to the Memo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, he here chuseth a Similitude to conclude his excellent Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon upon the Mount. The <ns0:hi>Builder</ns0:hi> intended, who our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour dignifieth with the name of a Wise Man; is, <ns0:hi>He that does not only hear Christ's Sayings, but doth them</ns0:hi>; under the Notion of hearing is comprehended, <ns0:hi>understanding</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving</ns0:hi> them, by <ns0:hi>doing</ns0:hi> them, he understandeth a <ns0:hi>sincere De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sire and Indeavour to do them,</ns0:hi> with a Practice so far as Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane frailty will permit. <ns0:hi>The House</ns0:hi> intended, seems to be <ns0:hi>an Hope for eternal Life and Salvation,</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Rock</ns0:hi> is meant Christ, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.4. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.20. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.4. Every wise Christian, before he buildeth up to himself an Hope of eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Life and Salvation through Christ, must find that he is one who doth not only read, and hear the word of God, but so hears as to understand and believe them, that with an Operative Faith, working upon his Soul to the Obedience of the Will of God, or at least a sincere Inde<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>vour to it. And he who doth so, tho his <ns0:hi>Hope</ns0:hi> may be sometimes as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />saulted with <ns0:hi>Fears, Doubts, Temptations,</ns0:hi> (which are like the Assaults of an House builed on a <ns0:hi>Rock,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Winds, Floods,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Storms</ns0:hi>) yet it shall not fail, because it is truly founded on Christ, according to the Revelation of his Will, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 10.28. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.3.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doth them not, shall be likened to a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell, and great was the fall of it.<ns0:note place="bottom">There are, and will be others, that as foolish Builders, run up an House in haste without looking to the Goodness of the Foundation, and happen to build it upon loose Ground: So they flatter themselves, with the <ns0:hi>Hopes</ns0:hi> of the House in the Heavens not made with Hands, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.1. without looking to the bottom and Foundation of these Hopes, whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther they be such as Christ hath warranted or no; but either, build their Hopes upon Gods infinite Mercy, or the suffici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ency of Christ's merits, or their own works, hearing the word of God, and performing some other Duties of Religi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, never regarding to live to the Obedience of the Will of God. And the same Event will be to these Men as to such foolish Builders, their B<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ilding may stand a while, but when a day of Visitation<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or Death, or sharp Afflictions or Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation comes, then their House, their Hopes, all fail and pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rish in a Moment: Because they had no good Foundation, <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 8.13, 14. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.20. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 27.8. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 11.7. <ns0:hi>and great will be the Fall of it.</ns0:hi> Their Misery and Calamity shall be the greater, by how much their <ns0:hi>Hopes</ns0:hi> hath been the stronger, the disappointment of their Expectation adding to their Misery.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 1.22. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 6.2. Luk. 4.32.</ns0:note> the people were astonished at his doctrine.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 For he taught them as one having autho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity, and not as the scribes.<ns0:note place="bottom">The same words also are repeated, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.22. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.32. They declare the Effect of this, and other of our Saviours Sermons, upon the Hearts of those that heard him, and the reason of it. <ns0:hi>They</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>astonished,</ns0:hi> affected with an <ns0:hi>Admi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration</ns0:hi> at what they heard him in this, and other Sermons deliver; the Divine Verities revealed in his Discourses, the pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity of his Doctrine, the convincing Power that attended it, his bold and free Speech without r<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>spect of Persons, the Sim<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plicity of his Phrase, the Gravity of his Matter: The Majesty he shewed in his Discourses affected the People, and made him appear to them, one sent of God and Clothed with his Authority. He did not teach as the <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> the ordinary Teachers amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews, from whom</ns0:hi> they had the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courses about <ns0:hi>Traditions,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rites,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ceremonies, Cold,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>dull Discourses,</ns0:hi> of little or no Tendency, to their <ns0:hi>eternal Salvation.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
